epic.name: Unified Web Portal Consolidation
epic.description: Consolidate 8 fragmented web portals into a single, unified, modular web portal for Claude Flow Novice with real-time agent monitoring, control, and visualization
epic.business_value: Reduce 714MB to ~300MB, eliminate 45% code duplication, provide consistent UX, enable 2-3x faster feature development

documentation_structure.description: This master configuration serves as the single source of truth for the Unified Web Portal Epic. It provides high-level overview, phase summaries, and clear references to detailed implementation documentation.

usage_instructions.starting_point: Read THIS FILE (epic-master-config.json) first for complete epic overview

detailed_implementation.step_2: Read sprint implementation plan JSON for technical specs (e.g., sprint-1.1-implementation-plan.json)
detailed_implementation.step_3: Follow sprint execution roadmap for step-by-step instructions (e.g., sprint-1.1-execution-roadmap.md)
detailed_implementation.step_4: Consult supporting documents as needed (feature matrix, migration guide)

key_issues: 670MB node_modules in src/web/frontend bloating main package
5 separate WebSocket implementations with inconsistent APIs
No shared component library - copy/paste development

structure: src/client/ - React frontend (Vite + React 18 + Material-UI v6)

packages/web-components.purpose: Reusable React components extracted from 8 portals

execution_instructions.overview: This epic follows a phase-by-phase approach, with each phase containing multiple sprints. Each sprint has detailed implementation plans and execution roadmaps.

starting_point.step_1: Read this master config file (epic-master-config.json) for complete epic overview
starting_point.step_2: Review current state analysis and target architecture sections
starting_point.step_3: Understand phase breakdown and sprint structure
starting_point.step_4: Proceed to detailed implementation using the workflow below

detailed_implementation_workflow.content: Phase guide contains sprint breakdown, architecture decisions, execution workflow, testing strategy, success metrics

step_2.action: Read sprint implementation plan JSON for technical specifications
step_2.content: Implementation plan contains detailed tasks, file templates, migration steps, acceptance criteria, validation commands

step_3.action: Follow sprint execution roadmap for step-by-step instructions
step_3.content: Execution roadmap contains bash commands, git workflow, troubleshooting, and sequential steps

file_hierarchy.level_1_master: epic-master-config.json (THIS FILE) - High-level overview with inline sprint summaries
file_hierarchy.level_2_phase: PHASE-N-CONSOLIDATED-GUIDE.md - Phase execution guide with sprint breakdown
file_hierarchy.level_5_supporting: Feature matrix, migration guide, quick start - Reference documentation

git_workflow.branch_strategy: Create feature branch per phase (e.g., feature/phase-1-foundation)
git_workflow.commit_strategy: Commit after each sprint completion with descriptive message
git_workflow.push_strategy: Push to remote after phase validation complete
example_commits: feat(phase-1): Complete Sprint 1.2 - Shared Component Library
feat(phase-1): Complete Sprint 1.3 - Unified Data Layer

qualitative.code_maintainability: Single source of truth for components

risk_1.mitigation: Provide migration guide, deprecation warnings, backward compatibility layer for v2.x

risk_2.mitigation: Extensive performance testing, React.memo, virtual scrolling, lazy loading

risk_3.mitigation: Comprehensive feature matrix, user testing, parallel deployment during transition
risk_3.contingency: Roll back to old portals if critical features missing

risk_4.mitigation: Phased delivery, MVP scope, regular stakeholder updates, buffer time in estimates
risk_4.contingency: Prioritize core features, defer nice-to-have features to v3.1

risk_5.mitigation: Use npm-check-updates to find compatible versions, test thoroughly with npm ls
risk_5.contingency: Keep separate package.json files temporarily and migrate gradually
